title: How to Fix CVE-2026-110264 in GitLab: Patch and Verify
summary: Fix CVE-2026-110264 in GitLab CE/EE: affected and fixed versions, upgrade steps, workaround limits, patch verification, and scoped Ruby regression evidence.

# How to fix CVE-2026-110264 in GitLab: patch and verification guide


Written by


[Rene Brandel](https://linkedin.com/in/renebrandel)


on


Sat Oct 31 2026


**To fix CVE-2026-110264, upgrade affected self-managed GitLab Community Edition (CE) or Enterprise Edition (EE) to a patched GitLab release through the supported upgrade path.** The minimum fixed versions are 18.11.13, 19.0.10, 19.1.9, 19.2.9, 19.3.6, 19.4.3 and 19.5.1. Verify the version actually running on every relevant node after the update; updating system Ruby alone is not proof that GitLab is patched.


[GitLab’s security advisory](https://docs.gitlab.com/releases/patches/patch-release-gitlab-19-5-1-released/) describes a regular-expression compiler integer overflow that can, under certain conditions, permit unauthenticated remote code execution. GitLab assigns CVSS 3.1 severity 10.0 and says GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated are already patched.


**Dates and scope:** the[CVE record](https://casco.com/cve/CVE-2026-110264) was published on **October 22, 2026** . Sources were checked and the defensive lab was run on **October 31, 2026** . The lab tested two upstream Ruby compiler regressions; it did **not** test exploitation or perform a GitLab upgrade. The operational instructions below come from vendor documentation.


## Affected GitLab versions and the first fixed releases


The[vendor advisory](https://docs.gitlab.com/releases/patches/patch-release-gitlab-19-5-1-released/) lists these affected ranges for both CE and EE. It does not restrict this CVE to one installation method.


Affected GitLab release range First release fixing this CVE


7.0 through 18.11.x, before 18.11.13 **18.11.13**


19.0.x before 19.0.10 **19.0.10**


19.1.x before 19.1.9 **19.1.9**


19.2.x before 19.2.9 **19.2.9**


19.3.x before 19.3.6 **19.3.6**


19.4.x before 19.4.3 **19.4.3**


19.5.x before 19.5.1 **19.5.1**


These are minimum fixes for this vulnerability, not a recommendation to remain on an unsupported branch. Select a supported, patched release and follow[GitLab’s required upgrade stops](https://docs.gitlab.com/update/upgrade_paths/) . Do not jump directly from an old major version to 19.5.1.


## 1. Check whether your GitLab installation is affected


Inventory self-managed instances, edition, installation method and the running GitLab application version. For Linux package installations, run this read-only check on each node running GitLab Rails, as described in the[maintenance documentation](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/raketasks/maintenance/) :


```text
sudo   gitlab-rake   gitlab:env:info
```


Compare the **GitLab version** with the table above. A scanner finding or a shell’s` ruby --version` is not enough:[GitLab patched the Ruby it ships](https://www.ruby-lang.org/en/news/2026/10/23/regexp-fixes-for-gitlab-cves/) , and vendor packages can include backported runtime fixes. For source builds or custom images, record the exact build and runtime patch provenance. If that provenance is unclear, keep remediation unverified and consult the vendor.


Checking exposure here means identifying affected software and deployment scope. It does not establish whether an attacker can reach a particular compilation path or whether an instance was previously compromised.


## 2. Back up and plan the upgrade


Follow[GitLab’s upgrade preparation](https://docs.gitlab.com/update/plan_your_upgrade/) : check version compatibility, required intermediate releases, available space and background migration completion. Back up application data, configuration and secrets. Test restoration and the upgrade in staging, and plan downtime or the documented multi-node sequence for your deployment.


The Ruby pilot described below did not validate these operational steps. Use the instructions for your own topology and version; a successful compiler regression test is not an application upgrade rehearsal.


## 3. Patch the GitLab package or image you actually deploy


Use the vendor procedure for your installation method:[Linux package](https://docs.gitlab.com/update/package/) ,[Docker](https://docs.gitlab.com/update/docker/) ,[Helm chart](https://docs.gitlab.com/charts/installation/upgrade/) or[self-compiled GitLab](https://docs.gitlab.com/update/upgrading_from_source/) . For Helm, map the chart release to the underlying GitLab version; the two version numbers are different.


Update the deployed artifact and all required nodes. Rebuilding an unused image or updating only the host Ruby does not establish that the GitLab service is patched.


### Example: Ubuntu/Debian, single-node Linux package, GitLab 19.5.x


**Use this example only after confirming the installation method, edition, backups, compatibility and upgrade prerequisites.** It illustrates the minimum 19.5.1 fix for an existing 19.5.x installation using[GitLab’s package syntax](https://docs.gitlab.com/update/package/) . Choose the command matching the installed edition; a later supported patch is preferable when available.


Refresh the configured package index:


```text
sudo   apt-get   update
```


For **Community Edition only** :


```text
sudo   apt-get   install   gitlab-ce=19.5.1-ce.0
```


For **Enterprise Edition only** , use this instead of the CE command:


```text
sudo   apt-get   install   gitlab-ee=19.5.1-ee.0
```


Other branches, operating systems, containers and multi-node deployments need their own target version and procedure. Complete the vendor’s migration and restart steps before validating the running deployment.


## 4. Verify remediation after the GitLab upgrade


1. **Verify the running release.** Re-run the GitLab version check on every Rails node. Confirm that each deployed package or image corresponds to a patched release, including workers and replicas in your deployment. Retain version output, package identity or image digest, node inventory and change timestamp.
2. **Verify operational health.** Check background migration completion and perform the[post-upgrade checks](https://docs.gitlab.com/update/plan_your_upgrade/) . For Linux packages, the[sanitized configuration check](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/raketasks/maintenance/) is` sudo gitlab-rake gitlab:check SANITIZE=true` .
3. **Exercise representative workflows.** Confirm sign-in, repository clone/push and a representative CI job using authorized test accounts. Investigate new errors and preserve the results with the change record.


[Health endpoints](https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/monitoring/health_check/) and` gitlab:check` show operational health; they do not prove this CVE is fixed. A clean scanner result alone is also insufficient. Patch verification needs running-version or build evidence tied to the vendor fix. It does not establish that an earlier compromise did not occur.


## Mitigation and workaround limits


The durable remediation is a patched GitLab release. As temporary containment, operators can evaluate restricting instance access to trusted networks while arranging the update. This is access reduction, **not a vendor-validated fix** ; it does not eliminate risk from users or systems that retain access.


[Ruby’s advisory](https://www.ruby-lang.org/en/news/2026/10/23/regexp-fixes-for-gitlab-cves/) explicitly says **` Regexp.timeout` does not protect against these compilation bugs** , and pattern-length limits are not reliable protection. For custom Ruby applications, it recommends avoiding compilation of untrusted regular expressions when an upgrade is unavailable. That is an application design change, not a universal GitLab configuration switch.


## Defensive test evidence: Ruby 3.4.11 versus 3.4.12


On October 31, 2026, the defensive pilot built minimal Ruby interpreters (` miniruby` ) from the official[Ruby 3.4.11](https://www.ruby-lang.org/en/news/2026/09/23/ruby-3-4-11-released/) and[Ruby 3.4.12](https://www.ruby-lang.org/en/news/2026/10/23/ruby-3-4-12-released/) source archives in a disposable remote sandbox. Each archive was checked against its publisher’s SHA256 sum.


The test ran a normal regexp control and two public compiler regression cases from Ruby 3.4.12’s` test/ruby/test_regexp.rb` , associated with[upstream fix #16801](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/pull/16801/files) . No full GitLab deployment was installed.


Test Ruby 3.4.11 Ruby 3.4.12


Normal regexp functionality control Passed Passed


` test_too_many_range_repeat` Accepted input Rejected with` RegexpError` :` too many range repeat`


` test_too_many_null_check` Accepted input Rejected with` RegexpError` :` too many null check`


**What this establishes:** the patched upstream interpreter rejects these two regression inputs while normal regexp functionality still passes the control.


**What it does not establish:** this is not an RCE demonstration, proof that a particular GitLab server is exploitable, validation of a full GitLab package/image upgrade, migrations or restart, or evidence that an entire application is secure. The operational guidance above is vendor-documented, not lab-validated.


The sandbox used Ubuntu 26.04.1, x86_64, GCC 15.2.0, two vCPUs and 4 GiB RAM. Each test had a 10-second CPU limit, 15-second wall limit and 1 GiB address-space cap, with core dumps disabled. Outbound network access and DNS were blocked during build and tests. No production data, credentials or public route were supplied. The nonpersistent session was stopped and cleanup verified.


[Download the machine-readable evidence](https://casco.com/blog/cve-2026-110264-gitlab-remediation/evidence.json) for source hashes, build commands, test results and limitations. It contains no exploit input. This is a scoped defensive test record, not an independent audit or a claim of human review.


## Frequently asked questions


### Which GitLab version fixes CVE-2026-110264?


The first fixes are **18.11.13, 19.0.10, 19.1.9, 19.2.9, 19.3.6, 19.4.3 and 19.5.1** . Choose a supported patched release and follow the upgrade path for your current branch. These thresholds come from the[GitLab advisory](https://docs.gitlab.com/releases/patches/patch-release-gitlab-19-5-1-released/) .


### Does updating system Ruby fix GitLab?


Not by itself.[Ruby identifies 4.0.9, 3.4.12 and 3.3.13](https://www.ruby-lang.org/en/news/2026/10/23/regexp-fixes-for-gitlab-cves/) as upstream releases containing these fixes and explains that GitLab patched the Ruby it ships. Verify the installed GitLab release or a documented vendor backport. For a separately maintained Ruby application, verify the runtime actually used by running processes after deployment.


### How do I verify that remediation is complete?


Retain evidence tying every running GitLab node and deployed artifact to a vendor-fixed release, then confirm migrations, service health and representative workflows. Keep unknown builds or nodes open. A passing health check, an updated local Ruby or a clean scan alone is not proof of remediation.


### Can I mitigate this CVE without upgrading?


Access restrictions can reduce exposure while you arrange the patch, but they do not repair the compiler. Ruby says matching timeouts and pattern-length limits are insufficient. Avoiding untrusted regexp compilation can help a custom application; do not assume GitLab offers a complete configuration workaround.


For the current source description and advisory references, see the[CVE-2026-110264 record](https://casco.com/cve/CVE-2026-110264) . The[CVE catalog](https://casco.com/cve) and[agent reference](https://casco.com/cve/agents) provide related lookup tools; they do not replace deployment verification.
